question: Which of the following structural modifications causes a morphine derivative to behave as an opioid (or opiate) receptor antagonist ?:

options.opa: A phenethyl group in the nitrogen and methylation of the hydroxyl in C-3.
options.opb: Oxidation of the hydroxyl in C-6 to ketone.
options.opc: An allyl group on nitrogen and a hydroxyl on C-14.
options.opd: Suppression of the double bond C7 = C8.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: A phenethyl group in the nitrogen -> methylation of the hydroxyl in C-3 -> morphine derivative behaves as an opioid receptor antagonist -> 80%
CHAIN: Oxidation of the hydroxyl in C-6 to ketone -> morphine derivative behaves as an opioid receptor antagonist -> 70%
CHAIN: An allyl group on nitrogen -> hydroxyl on C-14 -> morphine derivative behaves as an opioid receptor antagonist -> 75%
CHAIN: Suppression of the double bond C7 = C8 -> morphine derivative behaves as an opioid receptor antagonist -> 70%
